summary: Static site: Astro (web), hosted on Cloudflare Pages — Cloudflare edge network. Estimated $0-5/month.

frontend.justification: Web: Astro — Team already writes css, html, javascript for the UI; server-rendered/static HTML that search engines index; pre-built static pages, no server needed; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good fast delivery (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Astro is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 4/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 1.6 points behind. Known limit of Hugo: go templating is unfamiliar to JS developers.

Needs a server runtime for a site that does not (project.type). Astro is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 5/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 17.2 points behind. Known limit of SvelteKit: smaller hiring pool than React.

backend.justification: No application server is needed: there are no accounts, payments, uploads or dynamic data; pages are pre-built at deploy time.

alternatives.why_not: nothing to compute at request time for this site
a server to run and pay for with no feature that needs it

database.justification: Content lives as Markdown/HTML files in the repository; there is no user data to store.

alternatives.why_not: a single author edits files directly

hosting.justification: A static site needs nothing more than a CDN host; fits a zero budget on its free plan; fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good fast delivery (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Close runner-up (score 33.2 vs 33.6); a stable id-based tie-break keeps the result deterministic. Known limit of Firebase Hosting: spark plan: 10 GB storage and 10 GB/month transfer, site disabled when exceeded unless upgraded to Blaze.

Cloudflare Pages is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 4/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 1.6 points behind. Known limit of Amazon S3 + CloudFront: more setup than a git-push host (bucket policy, distribution, cache invalidation).
Excluded: self-managed infrastructure, but deployment_model is managed_cloud (infrastructure.deployment_model).

tradeoffs: 500 builds/month and 20,000 files per site on Free
No regional pinning of edge-cached content

what_would_change.new_choice: Amazon S3 + CloudFront (static site) — CloudFront edge (S3 origin bucket in your chosen region)
Firebase Hosting (Google Cloud) — Firebase global CDN

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Cloudflare Pages; free minutes cover a team of 1.

alternatives.why_not: equivalent; GitHub chosen for its marketplace of deploy actions

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.justification: The owner writes posts in Markdown in the repository; every push rebuilds and publishes the site.

alternatives.why_not: adds accounts and cost for a single author

tradeoffs: Non-technical editors would need a CMS later

assumptions: Hosting Cloudflare Pages: $0-0/month at the 'tiny' tier.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.
requirements.p95_latency_ms absent or null: no explicit latency target; typical web latency assumed.
Knowledge base as of 2026-11-10; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'tiny' from 3,000 users and ~50 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
